name: Eliashib
overview: Eliashib was a male Levite known primarily as the son of Joiakim. His identity is firmly rooted in the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for religious duties in Israel. Beyond his lineage, Scripture does not provide additional details or roles for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliashib means 'G-d restores,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's restorative power. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:10, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual resonance.
familyAndRelationships: Eliashib is explicitly identified as the father of Joiada and inferred to be the son of Joiakim. These family connections establish him within a priestly lineage important to the Levitical heritage. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Eliashib's significance in Scripture lies chiefly in his position within a priestly family during the post-exilic period. As the son of Joiakim and father of Joiada, he is part of the genealogical record that traces the restoration of the priesthood. His presence underscores God's faithfulness in preserving the Levitical line through whom worship and temple service continued.
